model: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF with finite-life terminal cap (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: 843,773,054 ordinary shares on issue at 31 July 2026 (FY26 AR note 23) plus 5,406,633 performance rights on issue = 849.18m fully diluted (ties to the FY26 diluted weighted average of 848.2m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The 2032 convertible notes (strike $7.41, above the current price) are carried as debt at face in net_debt and NOT also added to the count; converting them would only ever happen above $7.41. The DRP is satisfied by new issue (FY26 count +0.1%); immaterial and ignored.
inputs.net_debt_note: total_debt = convertible notes at FACE: $300.0m 2032 notes + $6.7m residual 2029 notes ($300m less $293.3m repurchased), lease liabilities ($146.6m) EXCLUDED under lease treatment B. cash = cash and equivalents 484.783 + other financial assets (short-term fixed-interest funds) 293.715 + term deposits 0.45 = 778.9. Company's own 'Net cash' of $482.2m (FY26 AR p.13) uses the notes' carrying value (242.7 liability + 53.6 option component); the $10m difference is capitalised transaction costs. Balance sheet 31 July 2026.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report note 3(b) share-based payments $6,730k; cash-flow reconciliation add-back $6,371k; no cash taxes on equity awards disclosed (nil). CSV StockBasedComp 6.731.
inputs.buyback_note: No shares repurchased in FY26 ($9.1m FY25, $192.4m FY23). The $100m on-market authorisation is unused; only financing-activity cash counts. Flat count is a modelling convention funded by the small SBC charge, not by buybacks.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-24T06:10:04Z (ASX regular close 24 Sep 2026; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.3% + beta 1.2 x 5.5% ERP = 10.9%, rounded to 11.0%. Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. No ad-hoc coal or cyclicality premium: thermal-coal price cyclicality, approval risk and decarbonisation are charged ONCE, in the probability-weighted scenario flows and the finite-life terminal caps, not in the discount rate. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. FY26 lease cash = principal 12.287 + interest 6.551 = $18.8m (1.07% of revenue); lease liabilities jumped 93.3 -> 146.6m (mining fleet), so the forward charge is set at 1.3% of revenue (~$24m/yr) via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities are excluded from net_debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY26 total D&A 238.7m = 13.5%; ex-ROU ~12.5%) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Bengalla (80%) is an unincorporated joint operation proportionately consolidated: revenue, costs, volumes and reserves are all reported at NHC's 80% share, so there is no non-controlling interest in the P&L or the bridge. Malabar (25.97%) is equity-accounted: its results are NOT in EBITDA/flows, so its carrying value is added in the equity bridge (matching-asset rule).
inputs.mid_cycle_basis: Thermal coal is highly cyclical; no single year is a base. FY22-23 were the supercycle (realised A$/t >250, EBITDA margins 60%+); FY26 realised A$143.2/t on a gC NEWC average of ~US$119.7/t, FY25 A$157.1/t. The ten-year NEWC average ex the 2022 spike is ~US$105/t; NHC's realisation ratio (A$ realised / US$ NEWC) ran 1.20-1.37 across FY25-26 (FX + API5/ash discount). Base mid-cycle realised price A$135/t (~US$105 at a 1.29 ratio) from FY28 after a A$138 transition year; bull A$150/t (structural supply-shortfall thesis, ~FY26 level persists); bear A$115/t (2019-21 average, ~US$92). Costs: FOB cash cost ex royalties A$88.9/t FY26 (up 7.9% on strip ratio and diesel); modelled A$87-89/t through FY29 (New Acland ramp lowers unit cost, offsetting inflation) then +2.5%/yr; royalties ~8% of realised price (FY26 11.3/143.2). Volumes: FY27 guidance ~12.7Mt saleable, New Acland 4.0Mt FY27 -> 4.5-4.6Mt FY28 -> 5.0Mtpa, Bengalla ~8.3Mt (80% of 13.4Mtpa ROM run-rate) -> group 13.0Mt FY28, 13.3Mt FY29+. Revenue = volume x price + ~A$80m other (QBH third-party throughput, pastoral, hedging). EBITDA margins are the per-tonne margin x volume, cross-checked: FY26 (143.2-100.2) x 11.789Mt = 507m vs underlying EBITDA 514.3m.
inputs.finite_life_note: Marketable reserves at 31 May 2026: New Acland 212Mt (but 283Mt of the 399Mt recoverable needs approvals beyond Stage 3, i.e. only ~60-65Mt is approved, ~12 years at 5Mtpa), Bengalla 72Mt at 100% = 57.6Mt NHC share (~7 years at 8.3Mt, within an approval that runs to 2039 and a much larger resource likely to be converted). Elimatta/Taroom (232Mt) are unapproved exploration deposits given no value. The 10-year explicit horizon (FY27-FY36) therefore spans the currently approved life; the terminal is NOT a perpetuity but a low cap multiple on year-10 owner FCF: base 5x (~8 more years of flat flows at 11%: Bengalla reserve conversion plus part of New Acland beyond Stage 3), bull 7x (~13 years: New Acland extension approved), bear 3x (~4 years: Bengalla wind-down only, no new approvals). Gordon growth is set at 0%/+1%/-2% and never binds (9.1x at 11% WACC vs the 5x cap); the cap is recorded as binding in every scenario. Rehabilitation provision of $136.4m deducted in the bridge because a finite-life miner pays it.
inputs.notes: MODEL: mid-cycle owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row: operating company, cyclical, non-US; owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md), run through the Drivers/engine route. Chosen over a pure reserve NAV because NHC's two mines are producing, guided assets with a reported cost base; the finite life is handled with a 10-year explicit build plus a capped (non-perpetuity) terminal, and the reserve statement is the cross-check in finite_life_note. Not a peak-earnings DCF: FY26 (NEWC ~US$120) is above the ex-spike ten-year average, so base flows use A$135/t, below FY25-26 realised prices. FY26 reported FCF of 370.6m is flattered by cash tax of only 32.8m (instalments set on the FY25 base) against a 92.6m expense; a tax-normalised FY26 owner FCF is ~290m. Bridgeport Energy (oil and gas) was divested 12 Sep 2025 for a net cash outflow of 12.1m plus contingent bonding/working-capital facilities to the buyer (not modelled, immaterial). Analysis JSON quotes a web-sourced post-results price of ~$6.47; the Yahoo close at price_as_of is used instead. FY26 dividend of 40cps fully franked (interim 10c + final 30c) = ~$338m, more than double FY26 NPAT of 161m, paid from the cash pile; the DRP is in operation without discount.

equity_bridge.item: Malabar Resources (25.97%, Maxwell underground mine) at equity-accounted carrying value
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note 19; KAM impairment-tested; NHC paid $2.00/share for +3.00% in Sep-25 ($36.1m), consistent with ~$1.2bn Malabar equity. Malabar's share of results (-11.1m FY26) is excluded from EBITDA and the flows, so the asset must sit in the bridge.
FY26 AR provisions note: current 5.236 + non-current 131.189. Deducted at book because the model is finite-life (capped terminal), so closure is a real cash cost the flows never carry.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment (nominal price inflation on flat post-ramp volumes); not any CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All CAGRs are cycle-phase artefacts, not trends: the 3-year figures start at the FY2023 supercycle peak (revenue 2,754m, EPS $1.26, owner FCF 1,296m) and the 5-year figures start at the FY2021 trough (NEWC ~US$80, EPS $0.095). Equity CAGR is suppressed by $1.6bn of dividends and buybacks over FY22-26, not by losses. Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY21 235.3, FY22 1,058.5, FY23 1,296.1, FY24 259.7, FY25 237.4, FY26 351.4. Equity 5-yr (8.4%) vs revenue 5-yr (11.0%) is within 30%; equity 3-yr (1.2%) vs revenue 3-yr (-13.8%) diverges but both describe the post-peak unwind.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is 0.3-0.4% of revenue so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs differ only through the interest-income strip (38.5m in FY23 on the peak cash pile). Growth is not the valuation driver here; the realised price deck and the finite life are.

base.growth_rationale: FY27: 12.7Mt (guidance) x A$138/t + 80m other = 1,833m (+3.7%). FY28: 13.0Mt x A$135 mid-cycle + 82 = 1,837m (+0.2%). FY29: 13.3Mt x 137.7 + 84 = 1,915m (+4.2%). FY30-36: volumes flat at 13.3Mt, price +2%/yr nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Per-tonne: FY27 (138 - 89 cost - 11.0 royalty) x 12.7 + 10 = 493m = 26.9%; FY28 (135 - 88 - 10.8) x 13.0 + 10 = 481m = 26.2%; FY29 (137.7 - 89.5 - 11.0) x 13.3 + 10 = 505m = 26.4%; thereafter price +2%/yr, FOB cost +2.5%/yr, so margin drifts from 26% to 24% by FY36. Compare FY26 actual 29.1% at A$143.2/t, FY20 26.7% at NEWC ~US$67 (on a much lower cost base).
base.capex_rationale: FY26 capex 193.5m (11.0%) with the Bengalla Growth Project complete and management guiding a return to a 'more sustainable level'. FY27 9% (~165m: sustaining ~A$9/t x 12.7Mt = 115m + New Acland road works/Manning Vale West fleet 50m); FY28 8%; FY29+ 7.5% (~145m, ~A$11/t sustaining incl. periodic fleet rebuilds). D&A converges from 12.5% ex-ROU toward capex as the growth assets amortise; it only affects cash tax.
base.tax_rationale: Statutory 30%. FY26 effective 36.5% (non-deductible associate loss, permanent differences) and FY25 26.9%; FY26 cash tax of 32.8m was a timing artefact. No losses carried forward. Royalties are inside FOB cost, not tax.
base.wc_rationale: Coal producer: receivables + product stocks (564kt) exceed payables, so growth consumes ~5% of the revenue increase; revenue declines release it.

bull.growth_rationale: FY27: 12.9Mt x A$150/t (H2-FY26 Middle East gas-to-coal switching persists) + 80 = 2,015m (+14.1%). FY28: 13.5Mt x A$145 + 82 = 2,040m. FY29: 14.0Mt (Acland at 5Mtpa plus Bengalla debottlenecking) x 145 + 84 = 2,114m. Then +2.5%/yr price on flat volume.
bull.margin_rationale: (150 - 88 - 12) x 12.9 + 10 = 655m = 32.5% FY27; (145 - 87 - 11.6) x 13.5 + 10 = 636m = 31.2% FY28; unit cost falls with Acland volume; price and cost both +2.5% so the margin holds ~31%. Above FY26's 29.1% on A$150 vs A$143.2 realised and lower unit cost, but still half the FY22-23 supercycle level (60%+).

bear.growth_rationale: FY27: 12.2Mt (rail disruption, Manning Vale West access slips) x A$122/t + 75 = 1,563m (-11.5%). FY28: 12.5Mt x A$115 (2019-21 average, ~US$92) + 75 = 1,513m. FY29-33: +1.5%/yr price. FY34-36: volumes -5%/yr as Bengalla's approved reserve depletes with no New Acland extension (price +1.5%).
bear.margin_rationale: (122 - 90 - 9.8) x 12.2 + 8 = 279m = 17.8% FY27; (115 - 90 - 9.2) x 12.5 + 8 = 206m = 13.6% FY28; cost +2.5%/yr against price +1.5%/yr compresses the per-tonne margin from A$15 to A$12 by FY33 and unit costs rise as volumes fall, so margin drifts to 7.5%. Cash tax goes to zero when D&A exceeds EBITDA less lease; the engine floors it. FCF is near zero from FY28, so the bear's value is the balance sheet: net cash + Malabar - rehab.

scenario_narratives.base: Thermal coal mean-reverts to its ex-spike ten-year average (~US$105/t NEWC, A$135/t realised for NHC's API5/high-ash-weighted mix) after a A$138/t transition year. New Acland ramps on guidance (4.0Mt FY27, 4.5-4.6Mt FY28, 5.0Mtpa from FY29) once Manning Vale West is accessed in Q4 CY2026; Bengalla holds its 13.4Mtpa ROM run-rate (8.3Mt saleable at 80%). Group volumes settle at 13.3Mt. FOB cash cost ex royalties holds ~A$87-89/t through the ramp (volume dilution offsets diesel and strip-ratio inflation) then rises 2.5%/yr against 2%/yr price, so the EBITDA margin drifts from 27% to 24%. Capex normalises to ~7.5% of revenue (~A$145m) as the growth programme completes. Owner FCF runs ~A$230-260m/yr, a 5x cap on year-10 FCF stands in for Bengalla reserve conversion and partial New Acland extension beyond FY2036, and the equity bridge adds net cash and Malabar and deducts rehabilitation.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's structural-supply-shortfall thesis holds: ageing seaborne supply, no new Australian thermal approvals and gas-to-coal switching keep NEWC around US$115-120 (A$150/t realised FY27, A$145 mid-cycle rising 2.5%/yr). New Acland reaches 5Mtpa on schedule and Bengalla debottlenecks to lift group volume to 14Mt, dropping unit costs. EBITDA margins hold ~31% (still half the supercycle level). Capex settles at 7%. New Acland's post-Stage-3 reserves (283Mt recoverable) win approval in the early 2030s, justifying a 7x terminal cap (~13 years of flat flows). Maxwell (Malabar) ramps to plan and supports its carrying value.
scenario_narratives.bear: Decarbonisation and Chinese domestic supply push NEWC back to the 2019-21 average (~US$92, A$115/t realised) from FY28 after a weak A$122 FY27, while Cross River Rail possessions and Queensland Rail industrial action cap New Acland at ~3.5-4Mt and Manning Vale West slips. Diesel and strip-ratio inflation run at 2.5%/yr against 1.5% price so the per-tonne margin compresses from A$22 to A$12 and EBITDA margins fall to single digits by FY33; owner FCF is roughly zero from FY28 because sustaining capex and lease cash consume the margin. No New Acland extension is approved and Bengalla's approved reserve depletes from FY34 (-5%/yr volumes); the terminal is 3x a near-zero year-10 FCF. The value is the balance sheet: A$472m net cash, Malabar at A$352m, less A$136m rehabilitation. Insurers and banks continue to withdraw from thermal coal, so the cash pile is not re-rated and the 40c dividend (paid from cash, 2x FY26 NPAT) is cut.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: a single-commodity price-taker in a structurally declining commodity, with a history of decade-long approval fights at New Acland, and a bull case that needs both a sustained price above the ex-spike average AND post-Stage-3 approvals. Bull cut to 20% for that same conjunction. Base 50%. The base case is not the analysts' hold-rated ~$5.34 target because they capitalise FY26-27 pricing; the house base capitalises the mid-cycle.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a thermal coal miner on mid-cycle owner FCF over its approved reserve life with a capped, non-perpetuity terminal, the equity-accounted Malabar stake added at carrying value, and closure cost deducted. Never capitalise a coal-price year (FY22-23 or FY26) in perpetuity. Risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate. The market price at the FY26 print is capitalising FY26-27 realised prices and the 40c franked dividend; the house model asks what the asset base earns across a cycle and when it stops.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle price deck: every A$10/t on 13.3Mt is ~A$93m of EBITDA (~A$65m of after-tax FCF, ~A$0.45/share of base value at 11% over 10 years plus terminal). The base A$135/t sits below FY25-26 realised prices; if FY26 pricing is the new normal the bull case (A$4.5-5/share) is the right one.

Terminal multiple / finite life: the 5x base cap assumes ~8 years of flows beyond FY2036. A perpetuity at 0% growth (9.1x) would add ~A$0.75/share; a Bengalla-only wind-down (3x) removes ~A$0.30/share.

New Acland ramp: Manning Vale West access (Q4 CY2026) and rail capacity (Cross River Rail, QR industrial action) determine whether 5Mtpa arrives in FY29 or later; each 1Mt/yr shortfall is ~A$40m of EBITDA at base prices.
Cost inflation: FOB cash cost rose 7.9% in FY26 (strip ratio 5.1x at Bengalla, diesel +21.7%); the model holds A$87-89/t through FY29 on Acland volume leverage, which is a judgment.

Capital allocation: FY26 dividends (~A$338m) exceeded NPAT (A$161m) and owner FCF on a normalised-tax basis; continued distribution at that pace draws down the A$472m net cash the bridge counts, and further Malabar top-ups (A$36m/yr) recycle it into an asset valued only at book.
Rehabilitation provision (A$136m at book, NPV) may be understated for a full closure; and the Safeguard Mechanism / carbon cost (A$7.3m provision) rises from FY27 at Bengalla.
Convertible notes at $7.41: dilutive only above the strike; capped call (notional A$200m) partially offsets. Modelled as debt at face.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.77-6.61; FY26 year-end (31 Jul 2026) share price 5.19 per the annual report.
data_sources.financials: research/NHC.AX/Reports/NHC.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, AUD millions, FY2016-FY2026 annual + half-years) and NHC.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt: capital management table (p.13, net cash), operating KPI table (volumes, A$/t price and costs), note 19 (Malabar), note 20 (borrowings, convertible notes), provisions note (rehabilitation), note 23 (shares on issue), Coal Reserves statement at 31 May 2026.
data_sources.qualitative: research/NHC.AX/Reports/NHC.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-24): FY27 guidance ~12.7Mt, New Acland 4.0Mt FY27 / 4.5-4.6Mt FY28 / 5Mtpa target, Bengalla 13.4Mtpa ROM, Stage 3 rail-loop condition removed Oct 2025, Bridgeport divested Sep 2025, Maxwell opened Jul 2026.
